articles.title: 特斯拉司机开启 FSD 后睡着，车辆冲入封闭车道撞飞警车致加州两名巡警重伤
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，加州公路巡逻队（CHP）当地时间 10 月 15 日公布了一段行车记录仪视频。视频显示，一辆特斯拉在 80 号州际公路上高速驶入事故封闭区域，撞上停靠的巡逻车，导致车内两名警员受伤。这名 22 岁的萨克拉门托男性驾驶员告诉调查人员，事发时自己刚好已经睡着，车辆处于 Full Self-Driving（FSD）驾驶状态。公开报道显示，此次事故发生于当地时间 10 月 13 日深夜，地点位于加州索拉诺县费尔菲尔德附近、Air Base Parkway 出口以西的 80 号州际公路东向车道。此前约一小时，同一路段发生了一起致命交通事故：一名 19 岁男子驾驶一辆 2007 款本田思域，因不明原因失控，随后与一辆 2017 款雪佛兰太浩（Tahoe）相撞。该男子被送往医院后不治而亡。该起致命事故发生后，加州警方派了四名公路巡逻队警员乘坐三辆巡逻车在现场开展调查，并封闭了东向四条车道。据称，两名警员当时正坐在一辆道奇战马（Charger）巡逻车内，涉事特斯拉车辆随后穿过封闭路段的锥桶，以高速行驶状态追尾巡逻车。此次撞击过程被巡逻车行车记录仪以及现场另一辆车的摄像头拍下。撞击后，巡逻车被推向一辆参与事故现场清理工作的拖车。两名警员因伤势严重被送往费尔菲尔德当地医院，目前均已出院；而特斯拉驾驶员仅受轻伤。加州公路巡逻队在 10 月 15 日发布的视频及声明中强调，尽管特斯拉将这项功能命名为“完全自动驾驶”，但它并不是真正的自动驾驶系统。该机构表示，FSD 属于需要驾驶员保持监督的驾驶辅助功能，该技术并不能免除驾驶员安全驾驶的责任，并提醒驾驶员在道路上保持警觉、减速行驶，并在接近事故现场时注意避让。特斯拉驾驶辅助系统与停靠应急车辆发生碰撞的问题，此前已受到美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）调查。2021 年 8 月，NHTSA 针对多起特斯拉撞上停靠警车、消防车等应急车辆的事故展开调查，相关事故不少发生在夜间，现场设有警示灯、照明信号或交通锥桶。2023 年 12 月，特斯拉召回超过 200 万辆汽车，并通过 OTA 软件更新增加驾驶员注意力提醒及相关控制措施。类似事故此后仍有发生。The Verge 报道称，2024 年 6 月，一辆使用 FSD 的特斯拉曾撞上一辆停靠的富勒顿警车，当时警员正在处理另一起致命事故。此次费尔菲尔德事故再次将驾驶员监督机制、系统对道路封闭标志的识别能力，以及驾驶辅助功能的使用边界置于关注之中。相关阅读：《特斯拉 FSD 在欧洲引发质疑：被指频繁超速、违规超越》

articles.title: 特斯拉美国 Model Y 穿越高速隔离带致人死亡，驾驶辅助系统处于启用状态
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，据 Electrek 周四报道，特斯拉向美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）提交的事故报告显示，今年 8 月的一起碰撞事故发生前，车辆的驾驶辅助系统处于已启用状态。据新泽西州警方通报，当地时间 2026 年 8 月 22 日上午 8 时 31 分左右，一辆特斯拉 Model Y 沿新泽西州坎伯兰县文兰市的 55 号公路向南行驶时失控，在约 34.6 英里（IT之家注：约 55.7 公里）路段驶离道路左侧，穿过中央草坪隔离带并撞上树木，随后进入对向车道，与一辆迎面驶来的雪佛兰 SUV 相撞，导致 SUV 驾驶员、68 岁的菲利普 · 伊斯特曼（Phillip Eastman）死亡，特斯拉驾驶员和雪佛兰车上一名乘客受伤。公开报道显示，伊斯特曼来自宾夕法尼亚州斯普林菲尔德，生前曾担任当地学区董事会成员，并拥有近 30 年青少年及高中冰球教练经历，其中 17 年担任斯普林菲尔德高中校队主教练。事故发生后，当地公开报道主要将事件描述为特斯拉驾驶员失去对车辆的控制，并未提及 Autopilot、Full Self-Driving（FSD）或其他驾驶辅助系统。Electrek 发现，特斯拉在提交给 NHTSA 的事故数据中将这起事故与一份此前未被公开报道关联到驾驶辅助系统的致命事故记录对应起来。特斯拉在最新提交的报告中将涉事车辆标记为 2,021 款 Model Y，并在自动化系统的“启用状态”（Engagement Status）一栏填写“Verified Engaged”，即已确认启用 Autopilot 或 FSD 系统。不过，特斯拉报告没有公开具体使用的是哪一套系统，也没有提供足以还原事故经过的完整信息。特斯拉将事故叙述、软件版本，以及车辆行驶道路是否处于系统获准运行范围内等字段标记为“机密商业信息”，相关内容因此被遮蔽。按照 NHTSA 的常设命令（Standing General Order），如果涉及二级驾驶辅助系统的车辆在碰撞发生前 30 秒内启用了相关系统，且事故造成死亡等规定后果，汽车制造商就需要向监管机构报告。此次报告还记录了事故发生前车辆的速度为 60km/h，但这一数值可能只是事故前某个时间点的远程信息记录，不能直接视为车辆驶离道路时的实际速度。此外，特斯拉在报告中仅确认持有车辆的远程信息数据，并未勾选持有事件数据记录器（EDR）数据或车载视频，因此公开记录无法确认是否存在其他可用于还原事故的车载证据。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，奇瑞 JAECOO 宣布联合 Momenta，共同在法国巴黎完成了“首个无接管的凯旋门智驾挑战”。据介绍，相应 JAECOO 7 测试车搭载 Momenta R7 世界模型，从拉德芳斯出发，跨越塞纳河，途经塞纳河畔讷伊，进入凯旋门环岛及周边街区，全程约 11.38 公里。沿途覆盖无标线道路、12 个环岛出口、反常规的“右方优先”、多方向车流汇入、施工绕行，以及行人、骑行者交互等复杂场景。其中，凯旋门环岛汇集 12 条大道，路面没有清晰的车道标线。与常见环岛不同，环岛内车辆还须让行右侧驶入的车辆。周围车流交错，通行空间不断变化，车辆需要准确判断让行与通行时机，并选择通往目标出口的路径，被称为“最难魔鬼环岛”。最终，JAECOO 7 成功完成了相应挑战，官方称整段通行丝滑流畅，展现出媲美欧洲老司机的驾驶表现。后续搭载 Momenta R7 世界模型的 JAECOO 7 车型将在进行充分测试后，正式与欧洲用户见面IT之家注意到，奇瑞 JAECOO 品牌于今年 4 月正式进入法国市场，今年 9 月新车注册量达到 2,589 辆，市场份额升至 1.6%。本月 JAECOO 7 也登顶英国全市场车型销量榜首。

articles.title: Mathematicians say OpenAI doesn't understand its own Navier-Stokes proof
articles.content: OpenAI submitted a 166-page solution to the Navier-Stokes problem but apparently doesn't fully understand its own proof. Several groups of experts dispute the claimed methodology, saying the actual approach differs from what OpenAI described. And because language models are black boxes, where the underlying ideas came from will likely never be clear. articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，经典模拟经营 IP《牧场物语》最新作《牧场物语：特拉迪亚的回响》（Harvest Moon®: Echoes of Teradea）现已正式发售，Steam 国区标准版定价为 ¥ 170，支持简体中文界面与字幕。IT之家附游戏商品页（https://store.steampowered.com/app/3591180/Harvest_Moon_Echoes_of_Teradea/?l=schinese&cc=cn）。踏上前往奇幻世界特拉底亚的难忘旅程，在这里，宁静的农场生活与惊心动魄的冒险交织在一起！你在宁静祥和的花绽村中成长，而如今，你的生活即将迎来巨大的改变。神秘的迷雾从回音森林中蔓延而出，野兽在夜幕下四处徘徊，奇异的灾害也开始威胁这片土地上的各个村庄。本作在保留传统农场经营玩法的基础上，新增了大量冒险探索内容，核心特色包括：恋爱与关系系统：可结识 10 位（5 男 5 女）各具魅力的恋爱对象，加深羁绊并触发专属剧情，寻找共度一生的伴侣。动物伙伴系统：与不同动物伙伴建立友谊，每只动物拥有独特能力，可帮助玩家破坏障碍物、发现隐藏地点，探索世界秘密。全新探索能力：加入跳跃、攀爬梯子、沿藤蔓向上攀爬等动作，允许玩家探索此前无法到达的区域，结合移动能力与动物伙伴能力深入世界每个角落。村民委托系统：帮助村民完成委托，为特拉底亚发展贡献力量，收集快乐能量，越多的快乐能量可以帮助丰收女神更快恢复这片土地。岛屿生活：收集航海图发现遥远岛屿，寻找隐藏宝藏，探索全新区域，并与特拉底亚特有的稀有动物成为朋友。未驯服荒野：荒野中生活着狼、熊、老虎等野生动物，玩家需要时刻保持警惕，避免被发现，否则会失去收集的物品并返回农场。根据 Steam 商店页面信息，在 2026 年 10 月 15 日至 11 月 11 日期间购买游戏，可免费领取莫贝里奶牛包预购特典。需要注意的是，该游戏需要控制器才能游玩，不支持键盘和鼠标操作，完全支持 Xbox 与 PlayStation 控制器。最低配置：需要 64 位处理器和操作系统，Windows 11 Pro 64-bit 系统，Intel Core i5-7200U @ 2.50GHz 处理器（4 CPUs, ~2.7GHz），16 GB 内存，NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 显卡，DIRECTX 版本 12，需要 8 GB 可用存储空间。推荐配置：需要 64 位处理器和操作系统，Windows 11 Pro 64-bit 系统，Intel Core i5-12400F CPU @ 3.70GHz 处理器（6 CPUs, ~3.7GHz），16 GB 内存，NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 显卡，DIRECTX 版本 12，需要 8 GB 可用存储空间。游戏图赏：

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，开发者 Brendan Keogh 在 Bluesky 发文，截至 10 月中旬，2026 年登陆 Steam 的新游戏数量已达到 21388 款，超过 2025 年全年的总量。考虑到今年还剩约两个半月，而年末传统上又是游戏发布较为密集的时期，预计 Steam 平台 2026 年全年发布的新游戏至少可能达到 24000 款。如此庞大的游戏数量，也让 Steam 面临越来越严重的内容拥挤问题。按照目前的数据计算，Steam 平均每天约有 66 款新游戏发布，而 2025 年这一数字约为 55 款。大量作品涌入平台，不仅增加了玩家筛选游戏的难度，也可能让一些质量出色、但缺乏知名度的作品被淹没在海量新品之中。目前，Valve 正在尝试通过算法推荐和个性化展示改善这一问题。例如 Steam 近期便上线了“个人日历”功能，集中展示算法认为玩家可能感兴趣的 10 款游戏。这些推荐会参考玩家此前加入愿望单的作品，以及其过往的游戏偏好。然而随着新游戏数量继续增长，此类内容筛选机制也将面临更大压力。Brendan Keogh 警告，随着目前 AI“氛围编程”潮流进一步延伸，许多开发者能够在数小时内制作出模仿现有热门游戏的作品，进一步造成平台充斥大量低劣游戏。若 Valve 不进一步调整审核、推荐和内容管理机制，2027 年登陆 Steam 的新游戏数量可能超过 30000 款，进一步造成更多玩家与开发者之间的矛盾。

articles.title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
articles.content: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville's time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment” a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today's podcast. Byrne's new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, looks to categorize numerous “sleeping beauties” — ideas that were lost but then rediscovered. Besides Melville and Minsky, we also talk about the lost Roman recipe for concrete and we get into Byrne's thoughts on how to write a song and his own experience of having his music rediscovered by a new generation. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 制造商 Elevation Lab 宣布下架苹果 AirTag 消音工具，公开致歉承认“产品可能被用于秘密跟踪他人”
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，据外媒 Appleinsider 报道，配件厂商 Elevation Lab 发布公告，宣布下架旗下 AirTag 消音工具 AirTag Silencer，并就产品可能被用于跟踪他人一事公开道歉。据介绍，AirTag Silencer 旨在让用户永久摧毁苹果 AirTag 内置的扬声器，使其不会发出任何声音。使用时，用户需要先取出 AirTag 电池，再将追踪器放入专用固定模具，随后用锤子将一根销钉直接打入扬声器。Elevation Lab  声称，这种方式可以让扬声器彻底失效，同时不损坏追踪器的其他组件。Elevation Lab 在推出这款工具时，声称这是为了防止窃贼在失窃物品被找回之前发现并拆除 AirTag，例如用户可以将消音后的 AirTag 放在自行车上，以降低追踪器发出声音、被窃贼发现的风险。但尽管如此，Elevation Lab 还是招致了业界广泛的批判。面对相关质疑，Elevation Lab 现已将产品从官网下架，并发布道歉声明。公司表示，团队成员希望将消音后的 AirTag 用于防盗追踪，但最终意识到，它也可能被心怀不轨的人利用，使无法收到手机提醒的人更难察觉自己正被跟踪。Elevation Lab 还称，未来将利用相关专利，阻止其他厂商制造类似产品。

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

articles.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
articles.content: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.content: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.content: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

articles.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
articles.content: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

articles.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
articles.content: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

articles.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

articles.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
articles.content: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

articles.title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
articles.content: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

articles.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
articles.content: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.

articles.title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves. A common approach fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens, but aligning these features with pretrained semantic representations remains challenging under limited spatial supervision. We propose DK-VLM with Dual-Kernel Attention, which computes attention from both a visual token's input position and its geometric position in the scene. A semantic kernel retains the pretrained model's native attention and positional encoding, while a separate geometric kernel uses estimated 3D points and camera poses to directly modulate attention through point displacements and relative view transformations. Then, a learned gate fuses their outputs. Geometry thus enters attention as position rather than as fused reconstruction features. We further introduce Reference-Frame Composition (RC) supervision to train the model to update its reference frame across successive judgments. It provides stepwise turn and heading targets derived from verified single-step annotations. Among the compared methods, DK-VLM-8B achieves the highest average score across six spatial benchmarks and the highest overall scores on VSI-Bench (74.33) and ReVSI-32 (58.28). RC supervision further improves multi-step spatial reasoning, while the full model preserves general video understanding. Project page: https://sumuru789.github.io/DK-VLM-website/.

articles.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
articles.content: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.

articles.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
articles.content: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.

articles.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
articles.content: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. articles.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
articles.content: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production-like systems to deliver working solutions. FDE-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer's own success metric, normalized between 0 (unchanged system) and 1 (reference solution), with penalties for stakeholder interactions (messages, trial runs, and waiting time). An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE-Gym score of 0.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks (a score of at least 0.8 with no incident). Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0.8 or above on only 10. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers.

articles.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
articles.content: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.

articles.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

articles.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
articles.content: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. articles.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. During pretraining, image-space contact maps derived from tactile gloves, together with features from a frozen 3D geometry teacher, supervise the visual tokens; these objectives are removed at inference. In parallel, a tactile pathway encodes regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint therefore supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment. To scale this supervision, we build HumanTouch, a 1,000-hour dataset of full-hand tactile human manipulation, and pretrain Spark-0 on it together with egocentric video, robot data, and simulation. We also release SparkArena, which pairs vision-only simulated tasks with tactile-conditioned real-robot tasks on one dexterous embodiment. Spark-0 achieves the highest mean success rate on both SparkArena tracks and ranks first on all eight aggregate metrics of the Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark. Compared with vision-only pretraining on the same data and compute with touch discarded, retaining the touch of 1,000 hours of HumanTouch raises vision-only success on Ego Humanoid from 52.5% to 71.7%, and success on SparkArena-Real, where touch is also used at deployment, from 44.0% to 52.0%, indicating that touch serves not only as a policy input but also as scalable supervision for dexterous visuomotor pretraining. articles.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
articles.content: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code. We build this corpus by collecting open-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content. It uses execution checks, spatial measurements, and visual feedback to automatically evaluate and revise generated programs without human feedback during generation. Third, we conduct systematic empirical studies of 3D coding, establishing baselines with fine-tuned open models and deriving practical guidance through component-level analyses of our harness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning on our dataset significantly improves the 3D coding capabilities of open-source models. Notably, our 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design (3D Object) in pairwise human evaluations, when both are utilized by Claude Opus 5.5.

articles.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
articles.content: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

articles.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
articles.content: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.

articles.title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Path-Safe Target Reaching in Robotic Harvesting of Hydroponic Lettuce
articles.content: Robotic harvesting requires precise manipulation to ensure accurate positioning of the end-effector, especially in a constraint workspace. This study introduces the Path-Safe Approach Proximal Policy Optimization (PSA-PPO), a target-conditioned local reaching framework designed for robotic harvesting of nutrient film technique (NFT)-hydroponic lettuce in greenhouses. The proposed PSA-PPO preserves the standard clipped PPO objective while introducing a harvesting-oriented policy formulation that integrates target-conditioned observations, corridor-aware spatial constraints, trajectory-history-based safety encoding, and task-specific success criteria for constrained robotic manipulation. PSAPPO was trained entirely in Isaac Lab and successfully transferred to a physical UR10e robotic arm without any real-world policy fine-tuning. In a controlled physical benchmark against 150 scheduled targets, PSA-PPO achieved the highest reaching rate of 94.7%, outperforming Cartesian+TOTG (86.0%), RRTConnect (88.0%), and RRT* (80.0%), while reducing median RMS jerk by 39.8 to 73.0% relative to the classical planners during the final approach segment. A formulation ablation evaluated over 200 simulation targets demonstrates that path-safety and side-corridor shaping are the principal drivers of harvesting-compatible performance: removing either term substantially degrades strict success even when terminal endpoint accuracy is preserved or improved, confirming that optimization toward the endpoint alone is an insufficient objective for constrained crop-proximal manipulation. Finally, PSA-PPO was integrated with an RGB-D vision module and an end-effector and evaluated as a complete greenhouse harvesting system across 144 lettuce harvesting attempts, achieving 94.4% vision-guided target reaching and 86.1% complete harvesting success.

articles.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
articles.content: We develop a robust reinforcement learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes. Applying our framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer in a simulator calibrated to clinical data, we obtain generalizable and robust policies that substantially outperform the existing adaptive therapy method. In particular, we attain robustness with almost no loss of performance when the biomarker is accurate and the disease evolves as anticipated, and find that the resulting policy Pareto-dominates the existing method across a diverse array of scenarios. Our findings suggest that robust RL holds great promise as a principled methodology for learning reliable adaptive treatment policies.

articles.title: Illumination-Aware Active Perception for Spacecraft Inspection
articles.content: Harsh and rapidly varying orbital illumination introduces failure modes during spacecraft inspection. Existing planners rely on line-of-sight inspection metrics which perform occlusion checks against a known target and conflate geometric visibility with task-relevant information. These metrics overlook illumination effects including eclipse, self-shadowing, and specular reflection from spacecraft materials and tend to declare components as inspected despite the corresponding images lacking sufficient information. We propose an inspection-planning framework that replaces geometric visibility with a learned measure of camera information derived from a classifier variational autoencoder (VAE) that operates directly on the captured image. The encoder model is trained to classify spacecraft surface components from rendered patches, and its total latent variance is used to learn the varying illumination of said components, replacing binary visibility checks with a continuous, image-grounded quantity. We evaluate the approach by implementing a Guidance, Navigation, and Control architecture in a photorealistic physics simulator, and vary lighting and viewing geometries with multiple orbits. We show that, although all approaches successfully maximize their own objective, our approach results in better illumination: a mean brightness of $0.57$, with $81.6\%$ of observations above $0.25$, compared with $0.02$ ($3.0\%$) for geometric planning with an illumination band and $0.04$ ($6.0\%$) for purely geometric planning.

articles.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. Indic languages are spoken by over a billion people, yet evaluation awareness remains almost entirely unstudied in them. We test four instruction-tuned models from three families in five Indic languages alongside English. A set of cues varies whether the model is told that it is monitored and whether the monitoring is a safety test. Models refuse harmful requests more often when they are told that they are being tested. This increase appears in all four models and all six languages. In Indic languages, refusal of harmful requests rises by 14.4 percentage points on average. The test cue also brings Indic refusal of harmful requests level with English, but raises refusal of benign Indic requests from 6.9% to 11.3%. We release all 47,880 judged responses to support further work. These results suggest that safety evaluations in Indic languages may not reflect how models treat their everyday users.

articles.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
articles.content: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. Recent process-supervision methods aim to assign credit at finer granularity, but they typically anchor credit to either surface-level trajectory states or model-internal signals, both of which become unreliable in deep search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy. We propose KnowGPO, a reinforcement learning framework that aligns trajectories by the task-relevant knowledge they have acquired rather than by their surface observations. For each query, KnowGPO decomposes the information required to derive the answer into atomic knowledge conditions, and represents the state of a trajectory at each step by the subset of conditions it has satisfied. Trajectories sharing the same knowledge state are grouped for within-group comparison, and the incremental knowledge gain between consecutive steps serves as an environment-grounded process reward. Experiments on Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA show KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome-only (GRPO) and process-supervision baselines (GiGPO, IGPO) by 3.8 to 4.2 points, with our 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open-source systems.

articles.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
articles.content: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing and calibration, and confidence-gated training self-conditioning. LangDiT significantly reduces generation perplexity in matched LangFlow comparisons, establishing a new state of the art in continuous language generation across different model formulations. Using LangFlow as a representative CDLM, LangDiT as a plug-and-play backbone leads to a new state-of-the-art model with a generation perplexity (GenPPL) of 21.72 using 1024 NFEs and 44.72 GenPPL using 128 NFEs on the unconditional generation of 1024-token sequences on the OpenWebText dataset. When adapted to Plaid-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT results in a new leading GenPPL of 11.33 using 1024 denoising NFEs, and 27.51 GenPPL using 128 denoising NFEs. These gains are achieved while retaining each model's underlying representation, training objective, and inference sampler, isolating transformer architecture as a fundamental source of improvement. Our study identifies architectural design as an important source of improvement in continuous diffusion language models.

articles.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
articles.content: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing. The main challenge is that self-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence.
